title: Churn Suppressor: Codegen & Refactor Eval Pack (2026)
summary: Working pack of prompts, scenarios, datasets, and runner instructions to catch regressions introduced by model updates that increase 'refactor churn' — i.e., edits that change code shape but should preserve semantics and compilation/unit-test behaviour. Focused on compilation, unit tests, and style constraint adherence across refactor/codegen tasks.
background: Onboarding new model checkpoints often introduces more verbose refactorings or stylistic churn that passes manual review but regresses downstream pipelines (failing builds, flaky tests, bigger diffs). This pack is an explicit set of cases and evaluation steps to quantify churn impact and provide pass/fail criteria for model rollouts for codegen+refactor features.
objectives: 1) Detect increases in edit-level churn and compilation failures after a model update. 2) Measure unit-test preservation rates for refactor prompts. 3) Enforce a set of configurable style constraints relevant to customer repos. 4) Provide a reproducible runner and reporting template for PR gating and onboarding checklists.
scope: Domain: Python and TypeScript focused. Categories: small refactors (rename/encapsulate), API migration (signature changes), extraction/inline refactors, and generation-from-spec. Not covering large-scale architecture rewrites or non-deterministic code synthesis tasks.
dataset_composition: Corpus of 420 prompts across four buckets: 160 compilation-sensitive snippets (missing imports, typing), 140 unit-preservation scenarios (small functions with tests), 80 style-constraint cases (lint expectations, max-line-length, docstring formats), 40 API-migration examples (callsite updates + expected adaptions). Each item has: minimal seed code, target tests (when applicable), and a short reference explanation.
prompt_overview: Prompts intentionally vary instruction granularity: terse instruction, constrained-refactor (must keep variable names), preservation-first (must not change public API), and style-first (apply PEP8/TSlint rules). We include examples to exercise the model's tendency to reorder code, change variable names, or add benign but problematic scaffolding (extra wrappers that break tests).
example_prompts: Refactor this Python function to extract a helper while preserving the public function signature and all existing unit tests. Do not rename top-level function or change exception types.

Update the TypeScript callsites to the new API: `client.fetchUser(userId)` => `client.getUser({ id: userId })`. Preserve existing await/async semantics, and ensure compilation passes with the provided tsconfig.
Simplify this loop into a list comprehension but keep behavior identical and all tests green. Follow PEP8 max-line-length 88 and maintain docstrings.
Refactor into smaller functions and add type annotations (Python) for mypy strict mode. Do not change external module imports or public class names.
evaluation_workflow: 1) Checkout baseline and candidate model checkpoints. 2) Run the prompt pack through deterministic seeding harness (nucleus sampling disabled). 3) For each example: a) capture model outputs, b) run static checks (formatter/linter), c) attempt compilation/build, d) run unit tests (isolated sandbox), e) compute diff-size metrics and semantic-equivalence signals. 4) Aggregate per-bucket pass rates, churn deltas, and failure mode breakdowns. 5) Produce a report and gating decision (pass | warn | fail) based on thresholds.
runner_instructions: - Use eval-runner v2.1 (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-runner). - Use ephemeral containers with the provided Dockerfile (python3.11 + node16). - Timeouts: compilation 30s, unit-test 120s per example. - Deterministic generation: temperature 0.0, top_p 1.0, seed from example id. - Output artifacts: generated code file, linter output, build logs, test output, unified diff against seed. - Upload artifacts to the eval bucket with path pattern: evals/{run_id}/{example_id}/.
metrics_and_thresholds: Primary metrics: compilation_success_rate, unit_test_preservation_rate, average_unified_diff_size, style_violation_rate, semantic_equivalence_score (syntactic-normalized heuristics). Suggested rollout thresholds: compilation_success_rate >= 98%, unit_test_preservation_rate >= 97%, average_unified_diff_size delta <= +15% (vs baseline), style_violation_rate <= 2% absolute. Any single critical compilation failure on a core example => automatic fail.
automation_notes: We wire this pack into the model onboarding pipeline as an optional pre-gate. The harness supports incremental runs; maintain a baseline artifacts cache for quick delta computations. Add a lightweight quick-check subset (40 examples) for fast CI pre-checks and full pack nightly runs.
reporting_template: Produce an HTML summary with per-bucket charts (pass/fail, diff-size distribution), top 10 failure examples with logs, and suggested remediation notes (prompt tweaks, conservative decoding strategies, or post-processing transforms). Include a short executive verdict and recommended rollout action.
retention_and_reporting: Store run artifacts for 90 days for reproducibility. Persist summarized metrics indefinitely in the eval-metrics DB under tag 'churn-suppressor'. Attach run id and candidate checkpoint id to model onboarding PRs.
open_questions_and_todo: Decide whether to include Java examples (customer requests exist) — tradeoff runtime/infra cost.
Add a small corpus of ternary flake/potentially-flaky tests to detect nondeterministic regressions.
Design a lightweight semantic equivalence oracle for refactors that go beyond unit tests (e.g., property-based checks).
Coordinate with DX to add example prompts to the public quickstart for explaining refactor-safety guarantees to customers.
related_issues: INF-1423 (onboarding flaky refactor behavior), ENG-2897 (eval-runner deterministic seed bug), DOCS-776 (public quickstart mention)
notes: This document is intentionally a working pack: expect iterative additions. When adding examples, prefer minimal seeds and explicit tests so failure modes are easy to triage. Keep style constraint rules small and concrete to avoid false positives.
